passage.title: LOCAL BOY SENT TO DESERT CAMP
paras: Sneakers stolen from charity auction, court hears
A teenager from the city has been sent to a juvenile camp in the Texas desert after he was found guilty of stealing a pair of sneakers donated by baseball star Clyde 'Sweet Feet' Livingston.

The sneakers had been given to a shelter for homeless children and were expected to raise thousands of dollars at a charity auction. They went missing from the shelter on Tuesday and were found in the boy's possession later the same day.
Mr Livingston told the court he was 'shocked and saddened'. 'Those shoes were meant to help kids who have nothing,' he said.

The judge said the theft was 'a crime against the most vulnerable children in our city'. He gave the boy the choice of jail or eighteen months at Camp Green Lake, where, the camp's brochure says, 'hard work builds character'. The boy chose the camp.
A spokesperson for the shelter said: 'We are relieved that justice has been done.'
passage.source: Teacher-written for TGA in the style of a newspaper report, based on events in Louis Sachar's Holes.

markScheme.a: Stanley's (and his family's): the report gives only the accusers' side, so readers assume he is guilty; it shows how reports can be one-sided.
